slides.title: Knowles’ Andragogy Meets Critical Equity
text: Knowles’ Andragogy Meets Critical Equity

Malcolm Knowles (Classical Theory): Self-Directed: Adults resist imposed knowledge. Life Experience: Learners bring a rich reservoir of prior knowledge. Immediate Relevance: Content must apply to current goals.

The Equity Expansion (Modern Reality): Power Dynamics: Marginalization dictates who feels safe sharing. Psychological Safety: Trauma and socioeconomic status condition participation. Proactive Design: Inclusion removes barriers before adjustments are requested.
slides.speakerNotes: Knowles assumed an unencumbered, autonomous adult. In reality, mature students carry socioeconomic precarity, systemic microaggressions, or past academic scarring. We must design psychological safety intentionally.

slides.title: The Inclusion Marketplace: 5 Adult Learning Barriers
text: The Inclusion Marketplace
Time Poverty & Role Conflict: Shift work and unpredictable hours; Active parenting and intensive elder care.
Neurodivergence: High executive load for organizational tasks; Hidden exhaustion from autistic/ADHD masking.
Linguistic Diversity: The trap of hidden academic language codes; Exclusion via culturally specific examples.
Digital Divide: Reliance on mobile-only or shared devices; Low bandwidth impacting synchronous learning.
Schooling Scars: Past educational trauma in formal schooling; Persistent fear of academic exposure.
slides.speakerNotes: Frame these five barrier areas not as student deficits, but as structural interfaces. Every barrier represents an institutional design challenge that thoughtful pedagogy and Universal Design can solve.

slides.title: How the Knowledge Marketplace Works
text: How the Knowledge Marketplace Works

Step 1: Questions & Resources — Start with the 5 Barriers: Question Sheet: Each team and individual starts with questions covering all 5 barrier areas. Resource Pack: Teams receive resources describing their assigned barrier challenge and explaining solutions.

Step 2: Flipchart Poster — Build Your Marketplace Stall: Synthesise: Unpack the challenge and practical inclusive solutions from your team's resource pack. Create Poster: Produce a clear visual poster on flipchart paper to teach visiting peers.

Step 3: Explain & Explore — Host & Roam the Stalls: 1 Stays Behind: One team member remains at the flipchart poster to explain the challenge and solutions. Roam & Find Answers: Team members visit the other areas to find answers to the 5-barrier questions.
Goal: Return to your home team and share the answers gathered from all 5 barrier stations.
slides.speakerNotes: Walk participants through the three-step Knowledge Marketplace protocol: (1) review the 5-barrier question sheet and team resource pack, (2) create a flipchart poster explaining the challenge and its solutions, and (3) leave one stallholder behind to teach visitors while team researchers visit the other stations to gather answers.

text: Marketplace Task: Station Protocol (15 Mins)
3 Minutes Per Station · Rotate in Triads Across the 5 Barriers
Green Post-It (Inclusive Flow): Document what already works in your module. Capture practical front-line adjustments and inclusive strategies from your studio, lab, or seminar.
Amber Post-It (Institutional Friction): Document persistent institutional barriers we face. Pinpoint where policies, systems, or assumptions still create roadblocks for adult learners.

slides.title: Semantic Waves (LCT): Tacit-to-Explicit Bridging
text: Semantic Waves (LCT): Tacit-to-Explicit Bridging
Scenario: Sam, 42 (Carpentry) — Retraining while working; strong practical know-how, less confident with technical vocabulary & written explanations.

The Research: Legitimation Code Theory — Karl Maton (2013) Semantic Waves: Practical Know-How (High Semantic Gravity, Low Semantic Density) vs. Technical Theory (Low Semantic Gravity, High Semantic Density). The 'Semantic Flatline' Trap: Adult vocational learners often get stuck—either performing brilliantly on the workshop floor while failing written assessments, or memorizing textbook definitions they cannot apply in practice.

Complex Strategy: Reverse-Wave Bridging (3-Step Diagnostic Check During Practical Observation): 1. Down-Escalate (Concrete): Perform the task on the rig and explain in everyday workshop vernacular ('Check' tacit mastery). 2. Pivot (Concept Mapping): Pause at a critical threshold and replace two colloquial actions with industry-standard technical terms on a voice-note or post-it diagram. 3. Up-Escalate (Abstract Transfer): Ask a hypothetical boundary question ('What happens to [Technical Term X] if the system pressure doubles?') before writing a single sentence.
slides.speakerNotes: Introduce Karl Maton's (2013) Legitimation Code Theory (LCT) and Semantic Waves. Rather than handing Sam a glossary or sentence starters immediately, use a three-step Reverse-Wave Oral-to-Written diagnostic check during practical observation to determine whether his barrier is purely linguistic/literacy-based or conceptual.

Rather than handing Sam a glossary or sentence starters immediately, use a three-step Reverse-Wave Oral-to-Written diagnostic check during practical observation to determine whether his barrier is purely linguistic/literacy-based or conceptual.

slides.title: Semantic Waves: Bridging Practical & Technical
text: SCENARIO EXTENSION • SAM, 42 (MATON, 2013)
Semantic Waves: Bridging Practical & Technical

ABSTRACT & TECHNICAL (Low Semantic Gravity) — Avoid 'semantic flatlines' by riding the wave from workshop floor to written theory — CONCRETE & PRACTICAL (High Semantic Gravity) — Legitimation Code Theory (LCT)
1. Down-Escalate (Check): Observe practical task explained in everyday workshop slang.
2. Pivot (Decide): Swap two colloquial actions for industry terms via voice-note.
3. Up-Escalate (Act): Probe system changes verbally before requiring written prose.
Diagnostic Purpose: Separate literacy barriers from deeper conceptual misconceptions. CHECK → DECIDE → ACT
slides.speakerNotes: Walk through the visual Semantic Wave progression for Sam (42): starting with high semantic gravity on the workshop floor (1. Down-Escalate / Check), pivoting via voice-note concept mapping (2. Pivot / Decide), and climbing to abstract transfer (3. Up-Escalate / Act) to separate literacy barriers from conceptual misconceptions.

slides.title: Differentiated Pathways to Practice
text: Differentiated Pathways to Practice

Developing Practitioners — Focus: Concrete, low-prep inclusive teaching strategies. Action: Embed 2–3 ready-to-use techniques into next week's plan. Goal: Build confidence in proactive universal design.

Experienced Lecturers — Focus: Complex edge-cases balancing inclusion and professional standards. Action: Design a micro-evaluation to measure a novel adaptation's impact. Goal: Share evidence of curricular adaptation success.
slides.speakerNotes: Highlight that experienced teachers need space to wrestle with complex edge cases, while newer colleagues benefit from immediate, high-leverage procedural templates.
